excerpts: i Way of Life & Culture Kiribati has developed a distinct way of life shaped by its geography – 32 low-lying atolls and one raised coral island scattered across vast stretches of the Pacific Ocean. Although part of the wider Pacific family, Kiribati maintains a unique culture, language, and identity that have been preserved through generations, largely thanks to its isolation and strong community values. The traditional subsistence economy of Kiribati is closely reflected in the social organisation of family life. Families come together to form clans, or te kaainga, which operate under shared customs, responsibilities, and mutual support. eauty & Literary Ties Abemama offers a more secluded and idyllic escape, known for its tranquil lagoon and historical connections. Robert Louis Stevenson: The famous author of Treasure Island once called Abemama home, drawing inspiration from its serene beauty and peaceful environment. Traditional Living: Abemama is an excellent place to witness the simplicity of the traditional I-Kiribati lifestyle, including traditional canoe building and fishing methods.
